title: Light reveals internal motion in electron crystals and can trigger their melting

title: Video Pool shares analog-digital piece 40 years in the making
desc: One of the first things that Orima Bendisse when he started his residency at the Video Pool Media Arts Centre in the Exchange District was watch through the footage that he had gathered on video cassettes in Quebec’s Gatineau Park some four decades earlier. “It was a shock, for sure,” he shares with a laugh. “I didn’t recognize myself and my friends, too.” What he didn’t expect from those old tapes was that the quality was still intact in all its charming, analog fashion. Those tapes, which focus on the park’s trees as they fly by from a car window, have now been blended with similar footage that Bendisse captured digitally of the same park just a couple of years ago and rendered through various hardware and software at Video Pool as part of its Scott Leroux Fund for Media Arts Exploration. The analog is more organic than the digital one, and there’s more flaws in analog than in digital.
